fatal_errors: The material is incorrectly described as laser-deposited rather than as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with an L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.

The proposed 900 °C chloride environment is unrelated to the tested 25–100 °C deionized-water tribo-corrosion regime and is physically underdefined; an aqueous chloride medium cannot exist at 900 °C under ordinary test conditions.
The matched DS2205 comparator and rapid 1100 °C heating/quenching treatment are omitted.
The hypothesis misses the central non-monotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and increased tribo-layer disruption at 100 °C.
It predicts generic synergistic acceleration without reconstructing the observed lower wear, friction, and corrosion response of the HEA relative to DS2205.
The claimed phase-boundary galvanic feedback and possible doubling of loss are not established by the cited evidence.
explanation: The response addresses the broad concept of wear-induced passive-film disruption and proposes useful wear-only and corrosion-only controls, but it does not reconstruct the target experiment or its main findings. The target mechanism is a temperature-dependent competition among depassivation, repassivation, abrasion, and tribo-layer stability in deionized water, not a 900 °C chloride-driven galvanic cycle. Evidence E4 supports chloride-induced localized attack in an EHEA, and E3 supports oxide formation during high-temperature wear, but neither demonstrates the proposed coupled positive feedback under the stated conditions; E2 concerns a different laser-clad alloy. The pre-oxidation comparison is only moderately discriminating because it can alter hardness, roughness, and friction as well as oxide stability. A valid falsification test would need a clearly specified environment and direct electrochemical, wear-volume, and film-rupture measurements with matched surface and mechanical properties.
